findings.title: Unindexed `OR` branch on `retryCount` in `deleteMany` forces a full table scan and isn't scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders
findings.body:
In `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany`, adding `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` as a top-level `OR` branch without `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or `scheduled: false`) and without an index on `retryCount` has two consequences:

1. PostgreSQL cannot use the existing `@@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate])` index to satisfy `WHERE (method = 'SMS' AND scheduledDate <= ...) OR retryCount > 1`, forcing a sequential scan of the entire `WorkflowReminder` table on every cron run.
2. Because `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and `scheduled: false` are omitted from the second `OR` branch, this query will also delete non-SMS `WorkflowReminder` rows if they ever use `retryCount`, as well as any reminder that was concurrently marked `scheduled: true` after a prior retry failure (orphaning its Twilio `referenceId` so it can no longer be cancelled on booking cancellation/reschedule).

Deleting the reminder directly in the failure branches when `reminder.retryCount >= 1` (instead of incrementing to 2 and scanning for `retryCount > 1` on the next cron run), or scoping the condition to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false` with a supporting index, avoids the full table scan and unintended deletions.
